Montgomery County Tax Sale Information

Types of Sales

  1. Upset Sale

    Eligibility: Properties delinquent in real estate taxes for two years.

    Conditions: Sold subject to all existing liens. Buyers should conduct thorough research and consult an attorney.

    Advertisement: Local newspapers and the Montgomery County Law Reporter list properties within two months of the sale.

    Responsibilities: Winning bidders are responsible for transfer taxes and fees.
  2. Judicial Sale

    Eligibility: Properties not sold at the Upset Sale.

    Conditions: The county notifies lienholders properly and sells properties free of all liens.

    Advertisement: The newspaper and the Montgomery County Law Reporter list properties at least 30 days before the sale.

    Responsibilities: Winning bidders are responsible for transfer taxes and fees.
  3. Continued Upset/Judicial Sale

    Eligibility: Properties not exposed or sold at previous sales.

    Conditions: Similar to original Upset and Judicial Sales.

Additional Opportunities

If properties remain unsold after both the Upset and Judicial Sales, they may be available through:

  • Private Sale: Interested buyers can submit written bids for unsold properties. The Tax Claim Bureau decides whether to accept the bid. Purchasers assume responsibility for all liens on the property.
  • Repository Sale: Properties not sold at a Judicial Sale are placed in a repository. Bids start at $500, and properties are sold free and clear of all delinquent taxes and liens.

Tips for Bidders

  • Register Early: Ensure you complete your bidder registration on time.
  • Do Your Research: Thoroughly investigate properties before bidding. Since properties are sold “as-is,” understanding potential liens and other encumbrances is crucial.
  • Consult an Attorney: Given the complexities of tax sales, seeking legal advice can help navigate the process and avoid potential pitfalls.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What is an Upset Sale?

A: An Upset Sale is a public auction of properties that are two years delinquent in real estate taxes. Properties are sold subject to existing liens.

Q: What happens if a property isn’t sold at the Upset Sale?

A: It progresses to the Judicial Sale, where properties are sold free of all liens after appropriate notifications.

Q: Can I inspect the properties before bidding?

A: No, bidders do not have access to properties before the sale.

Q: What are the responsibilities of the winning bidder?

A: The winning bidder must pay all transfer taxes and fees and conduct due diligence regarding property conditions and encumbrances.

For more information and detailed conditions, visit the Montgomery County Tax Claim Bureau.
